title: Not everything needs a class
description: Classes are a tool, not a rule. Learn to tell when a dictionary or a plain function does the job more simply.

tasks.title: Choose the simplest shape that fits
tasks.body: A class earns its place when its data and its actions belong together, and several objects of that kind exist and change. When there is only data, a dictionary is enough. When there is only an action, a plain function is enough.
tasks.detail: Ask three questions. Does it hold data that changes? Are there several of them at once? Do actions belong to that data? If the answers are no, a dictionary or a function is easier to read and to test. Start simple: you can turn a dictionary into a class later, when it needs one.

tasks.note: Both heroes hold the same two facts, but the class adds nothing yet: it has no methods. A dictionary says the same thing with less code. heal() is a plain function: a number goes in and a number comes out, so it can be tested on its own. min() keeps the health from going over 10.

tasks.question: A program reads one settings record when it starts, and never changes it. Which fits best?
tasks.why: One record, no actions, no copies: a dictionary holds it with no extra code. A class would add a shape with nothing to do.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: give Hero a method heal(self, amount) that adds to self.health, and call nova.heal(3). Then compare it with the heal() function: which reads more clearly to you, and why?

Look back at programs you wrote in units 10 and 11, or at the example. For each part below, say which shape you would use, a class, a dictionary or a function, and why, with details from a real program. There is no single right answer: what counts is your reason. This is reviewed by you, and recorded as your own review.
hints: Look for data that never changes and has no actions: a settings record, one line read from a file, a single score. Those are dictionary-sized.
A class earns its place when several objects exist at once and each changes over time, like heroes that take hits and drink potions.
An action that only needs its inputs, like working out a price with tax, is a function. If you can test it with one assert and no object, it is a function.

criteria.text: I found data that does not need a class.
criteria.ask: What was it, and what would you keep it in instead?

criteria.text: I found a case where a class earns its place.
criteria.ask: Which data and which actions belong together there?

criteria.text: I found an action that works best as a plain function.
criteria.ask: Which action, and how would you test it on its own?
